I was very angry when I heard their outcry and these complaints. After thinking it over, I brought charges against the nobles, the nobles and the officials. I said to them, "You are all taking interest from your own people." And I called a great assembly to deal with them, saying, "As far as we were able, we have brought back our Jewish kindred who had been sold to other nations, but now you are selling your own kin who must then be brought back by us." They were silent and could not find a word to say. So I said, "The thing that you are doing is not good."

Should you not walk in the fear of our God to prevent the taunts of the nations, our enemies? Moreover, I, along with my brothers and servants, are lending them money and grain. Let us stop this taking of interest. Restore to them their fields, vineyards, olive work or orchards, and houses, as well as their interests on money, grain, wine, and oil that you have been exacting from them. Then they said, "We will restore everything and demand nothing more from them. We will do as you say." And I called the priests and made them take an oath to do as they had promised.

I also shook out the folds of my garment and said, "So may God shake out everyone from house and property who does not perform this promise. Thus may they be shaken out and emptied." And all the assembly said, "Amen," and praised the Lord. The people did as they had promised.

This is a really important aspect of the Jews that people don't understand how unified they are. For example, if you're a Jewish person, you can always get an interest-free loan from Jewish organizations to buy a house or start a business. If you want to buy a house or start a business, we go to the bank and they charge 10% interest, which may be unaffordable. But if you're a Jewish person, regardless of how poor you are, there will always be Jewish organizations that can offer you an interest-free loan.

When the seventh month came, the people of Israel being settled in their towns gathered together into the square before the Watergate. They told the scribe Ezra to bring the book of the law of Moses, which the Lord had given to Israel. Accordingly, the priest Ezra brought the law before the assembly, both men and women, and all who could hear with understanding. This was on the first day of the seventh month. He read from it facing the square before the water gate from early morning until midday in the presence of the men and women and those who could understand. All of the people were attentive to the book of the law.

So this is the last step of creating the Jewish identity. They follow the laws of God, do not marry outside their religion, and do not charge each other interest. Their historical memory is the Bible, which makes them extremely resilient because no matter where they are or how low their circumstances go, their historical identity is always stored in one Bible.

In those days I saw in Judah people treating wine on the Sabbath, bringing in heaps of grain and loading them on donkeys and also wine, grapes, figs, and all kinds of burdens which they brought into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. And I warned them against selling food.
